title: v2: behavioural feedback (quiet dot, pause nudge, conversation summary)
description: Why: docs/v1-lessons.md. Plan: docs/plans/2026-09-19-v2-behavioural-feedback-plan.md. A live wpm number becomes wallpaper and invites the guidance effect; the target behaviour is pausing. v2: dot only, pause nudge after 15 s without a pause (+ floating pill), slow-down cue from a 25 s average, end-of-conversation summary with calm/ok/rushed rating.

title: Installable menu-bar app: build script, .app bundle, launch at login, listen on launch
description: Rufus wants a tray icon he can leave running or toggle, without running a command before each call. Script: build release, wrap in ~/Applications/Speaking Speed.app (LSUIElement, mic usage string, ad-hoc signed), default to menu bar mode when launched as an app, menu toggles for Launch at login (SMAppService) and Listen automatically.

title: Live-test and tune rate estimate on real speech
description: First real-mic runs (2026-09-19) read 7.2 syl/s in the menu bar and ~12 syl/s off room noise when the window was mostly silent; typical speech is 4-6. Rufus to: run 'speaking-speed monitor', stay silent 10 s, then read a paragraph at normal pace; note floor/peak dB and rate. Candidate fixes if it overcounts: de Jong & Wempe relative threshold (speech = above p99 - 25 dB, nuclei above median), an absolute minimum speech level, or larger speechMarginDB. Then run 'calibrate' and a 10-minute call with headphones.
notes: 2026-09-19 resolved on clips: (1) displayed metric switched to speaking rate (in-turn pauses count) because Rufus speeds up mainly by dropping pauses; (2) detector retuned vs true syllable counts: smoothFrames=1, minDipDB=3, speechBelowPeakDB=35, minLoudDB=-35. Clips: slow/normal/fast true 3.6/4.5/5.0, measured 3.8/4.4/4.7. Remaining: calibrate + real call with headset; fixtures await Rufus OK to commit (repo is public).

title: Rewrite phase 1 plan for Swift (SwiftPM, terminal-run, no bundling)
description: Python plan is superseded (see design doc section 6). Produce a Swift task-by-task TDD plan: Package.swift with executable + test target, AVAudioEngine capture, Accelerate envelope, nucleus detection, metrics, zones with hysteresis, config (JSON in ~/.config/speaking-speed), NSStatusItem menu bar, session CSV + report, calibration. Port the Python tests to XCTest. Prereq: Xcode 26 installed (check: xcodebuild -version shows 26, xcrun --show-sdk-version shows 26).

title: Write up research: what the evidence says about speaking slower, plus recommendation and next steps
description: Dedicated docs/research.md suitable as basis for a blog post / landing page: evidence on speech rate, pauses, chunking, feedback and carryover; verdict on the app experiment; next steps.

title: Explain the number in README and app (what it measures, typical ranges)
description: Rufus: not clear to people what the number is. README: what speaking rate means, that pauses count, rough ranges (e.g. calm ~130-150 wpm, conversational ~150-170, fast 180+ once wpm lands), the 5-10 s averaging lag, that it is an estimate from loudness not transcription. In the app: a short 'What is this?' line or tooltip in the menu.

title: Show words per minute instead of syllables per second
description: Rufus: people know wpm, syl/s means nothing to them. Display estimated wpm = syl/s x 60 / syllables-per-word. English conversation averages ~1.4-1.5 syl/word; the fixture script is 1.69 (formal text), so pick a default (~1.5) and make it configurable. Reference point: Wispr Flow measures Rufus at ~180 wpm while dictating (fast). Label clearly as an estimate ('~150 wpm'). Update calibrate output, report, CSV (keep syl/s too), thresholds (store in syl/s internally or convert).

title: Shorter rate window (~5 s) so the indicator responds faster
description: Rufus (2026-09-19): 10 s window is too slow to respond to changes of pace. Try windowS=5. Trade-off: fewer syllables per window -> noisier rate. Check: replay fixtures/ through a sliding 5 s window (add a --live/sliding mode to analyze) and see how much the rate jitters; maybe pair with lighter zone smoothing. Note minPhonationS=1.0 and turnGapS=2.0 interact with a short window; the run-length counter needs its own longer history if the window shrinks below the calm run limit (12 s).

title: Speaking Speed phase 1: local rate + pause menu-bar monitor
description: Build the phase 1 monitor per docs/plans/2026-09-18-speaking-speed-phase1-plan.md (design: docs/plans/2026-09-18-speaking-speed-research-and-design.md). Python via uv, no transcription, no bundling.

First task: rewrite docs/plans/2026-09-18-speaking-speed-phase1-plan.md as a Swift plan; DSP design/tests/thresholds port directly.

title: Speaking stats over time: log and graph your speaking across the day
description: Someday idea (Rufus, 2026-09-19): record stats over time and show them, e.g. a graph of your speaking over the day: when you talked, how fast, fast stretches, long runs, pauses, how it changes across calls and days. Raw data already exists: per-tick CSVs in ~/.local/share/speaking-speed/sessions. Options: a menu item that opens a local HTML report, or a small SwiftUI window with Swift Charts. Needs a design pass first (what questions should the graph answer).
